decisions.reasoning: Daily trend is decisively up after the Aug 19 volume explosion (+18% on 71.7k, 3-4x any other day since May) broke a month-long 1840-1950 range. Eight days of sideways since, 2355-2565, holding well above the breakout — that reads as digestion, not distribution. Yesterday's flush to 2406 came on 13.2k volume but got zero follow-through: the next three 4h bars printed 590/642/701 volume and drifted sideways, then ticked up. I'm buying the lower half of a post-breakout range with the higher timeframe behind me. Stop at 2345 sits under the Aug 23 swing low (2355) — that's ~3x ATR, wide enough that ordinary range noise won't take me out, and it marks the level where "consolidation" becomes "failed breakout." Third is the max size I'm allowed, so I'm taking all of it.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a 4h close above $2,511 (the Aug 27 daily close, upper half of the range) before it prints any daily close below $2,380. If instead a daily bar closes under $2,380 first, the post-breakout consolidation is failing and I was wrong.

decisions.reasoning: My last prediction resolved as a miss on both legs — no 4h close over 2511, no daily close under 2380 — so the range simply refused to resolve inside five days. Price now sits at 2405, in the lower half of the 2355-2565 post-breakout range. Structure has deteriorated into a descending triangle (lower highs 2565/2534/2489/2428 against a flat 2355-2386 floor), which biases down, but the selling volume is ~21k/day versus the 71.7k that created the breakout and 30-60k that built the range. Fading volume into support reads as digestion, not distribution. My stop at 2345 already sits just under the twice-tested floor, so the position is asking exactly the right question. Selling here would cost 0.5% in fees to sidestep a 2.5% adverse move that is close to a coin flip, and would give up the bounce if the floor holds a third time. The decision was made when I set the stop; I honor it instead of churning.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a 4h close above $2,470 before it trades down to $2,345 (my stop). If the stop fills first, the Aug 19 breakout was a fakeout and I was wrong twice on the same thesis. If neither happens by the deadline, the range is still unresolved and I will treat the position as no longer justified by its original premise.

decisions.reasoning: Last call hit: 4h close >2470 printed on 09-05 (2477.82) with the 2345 stop never approached. The descending triangle I was worried about at wake 31 has inverted — 09-04's 2546.40 high broke the lower-high sequence, and daily lows have risen six sessions straight (2355/2370/2432/2445/2463/2466) into a flat 2525-2546 ceiling. Volume fading into the coil is compression, not distribution. I'm at the size cap so adding isn't available, and selling means paying a round trip to abandon a thesis that just worked with my stop 5% below the whole structure. Hold and let the coil resolve.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a 4h close above $2,546 (above the 09-04 swing high, i.e. the coil resolving upward) before it prints any daily close below $2,450. A daily close under $2,450 kills the six-day higher-low sequence and means the ascending structure was noise, not accumulation — that is me being wrong.

decisions.reasoning: My bullish structural thesis is dead — I scored it a miss and I'm not pretending otherwise. But the replacement read isn't "bearish," it's "range." ETH has chopped 2355-2665 for five weeks and today's high-volume flush to 2388 is the fourth test of a shelf buyers have defended every time. Two failed blowoff tops mean I won't add, and I'm capped at a third anyway, so the only live choice is hold vs sell. Selling here means dumping at the range low, three percent above a stop I placed below that low precisely to define this loss — that's abandoning a plan that hasn't actually been violated, and paying a fee to do it. All three of my errors so far came from acting with the most recent candle; selling this one would be the fourth. The stop does the work.
decisions.expectation: The 2355-2390 shelf holds again: ETH prints a 4h close back above $2,475 before it trades down to $2,345. If it reaches 2345 first, the five-week range has broken down, I get stopped out, and my range read was wrong. If neither happens by the deadline, price is drifting in the 2390-2470 dead zone and my call earns no credit. I also expect no trade above $2,665 in this window.

decisions.reasoning: Range 2355-2665 is in week six and ETH just thrust into its upper quartile on one 4h bar. The two prior thrusts into this zone (09-11 high 2664, 09-14 high 2614) both fully retraced same-day. My own record says my failure mode is reading thrusts like this as breakouts — three bullish-continuation misses, versus one hit when I assumed chop. So I will not add at the range top with a mandated stop sitting inside the noise band. I also will not trim: my 1/3 at 2452 is below range mid, it is the inventory I want when the range finally resolves, and shaving a third of it banks about $5 against real fees. Position unchanged, stop stays 2345 under the range floor. Tools returned zero bars on all three calls again, so this is prompt data only.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a 4h close below $2,500 before it prints any 4h close above $2,665. Those are equidistant from the current $2,582 (-82 / +83), so this is a genuine coin-flip framing and I am calling the downside: the third push into the range top fails like the prior two. If a 4h close above $2,665 comes first, the five-week range has broken out and my range regime read is wrong — and I will have been holding too little, not too much.

decisions.reasoning: My 09-18 range call is falsified: a 4h close above 2665 (2724.79) came first. The five-week 2355-2665 range is broken upward on real confirmation — 66k-volume daily engulfing on 09-18, a higher low at 2563, then a flag breakout on rising volume. Unlike the 09-11 and 09-14 thrusts, this one didn't round-trip the same day. Regime is now uptrend, 2665 is support. That argues for adding, and I still don't, for one mechanical reason: buying resets the stop on my whole position, and my stop band caps out at 2594.67. That would convert a position with a 15% cushion and a 12.9% gain into one that a routine breakout retest closes. Separately, I'd be buying the top candle of a +4.7% 3x-ATR vertical day, and my forward record on exactly that impulse is 0/3. I'm already 36% long and capture the upside without paying fees to chase. The add I want is 2650-2710 on a retest that holds, stop under 2595.
decisions.expectation: ETH trades at or below $2,680 before it prints any 4h close above $2,860 (equidistant from 2768.95 at -89/+91, so this is a genuine call, not a hedge). I am saying the breakout is real but short-term exhausted and the next move is back toward the breakout level. A 4h close above $2,860 first means I was wrong about exhaustion and under-owned a trend I correctly identified. A 4h close below $2,600 means the breakout failed outright and the range was not dead.

decisions.reasoning:
My 09-21 exhaustion call was right: I said price would revisit 2680 before any 4h close above 2860, and it has (low 2635 on 09-23). So the breakout is real but the buyers who made it are done for now.

Three straight lower daily highs and lower closes, and we are now back under 2665 — the old range top I called new support. The 09-23 12:00 bar dumped 70 points on 20.7k volume, and every bounce since has come on 1.8k-10k, i.e. shrinking. Weak bounces off a heavy-volume break means sellers still have the ball. The one thing still intact is the higher-low sequence from the 09-15 low: 2356 → 2434 → 2563 → 2635.

My standing plan was to add a third on a 2650-2710 pullback that holds. It did not hold — price is 2642 and still making lower lows, which is a falling knife, not a base. And the structural reason I did not add last time is worse now, not better: buying resets the stop on my entire position. At a 2642 fill the widest legal stop is 2467.73, which drags my whole book's stop up from 2345. Combined position would average ~2544, so a routine 6.6% dip to 2467 turns a 7.8% winner into a realized loss on both lots. I am not paying that price for exposure into a downtrending tape. Holding the existing third with an 11%-away stop lets it survive a full retest of the higher low, which is exactly what I think is coming.

Not selling either: 35% exposure, entry 2452, and nothing has broken yet — 2563 is untouched. Selling a winner into an ordinary pullback is how I pay fees to be flat right before the trend resumes.
decisions.expectation: ETH trades at or below $2,564 — a full retest of the 09-20 higher low — before it prints any 4h close above $2,720. Both are $78 from the current $2,642, so this is a genuine directional call, not a hedge: I am saying the post-breakout throwback goes all the way back to the last higher low. If a 4h close above $2,720 comes first, the shallow-pullback reading was correct, I misread the shrinking bounce volume, and I should have added in the 2650-2710 zone as planned. If price trades below $2,563 AND then a daily close prints under $2,540, the higher-low sequence is broken, the 09-21 breakout has failed back into the old range, and my uptrend regime call is dead — in that case I should be reducing, not adding.

decisions.reasoning: Four wakes of correct-ish range calls with zero added exposure while price rose 9%. The condition I set for myself — wait for a base to form — is now met: four days of 2627-2742 with volume collapsing from 47.6k to 11.9k, on top of an unbroken daily higher-low sequence (2356/2434/2563/2627/2636). Last night's probe to 2635 got bought back to 2668 inside one 4h bar. I'm buying the lower third of the base, not the breakout, which is the cheap location. The stop at 2547 is the widest the band allows and lands below the 09-20 higher low at 2563 — the level that actually invalidates the uptrend. My 8.9% embedded gain makes the blended book roughly breakeven at that stop, so a structurally correct stop costs ~3% of equity rather than surrendering the winner. 1.7:1 or better on a 230-point continuation. Staying at 35% exposure in a trend I've correctly identified is the mistake I keep making.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a 4h close above $2,742 (the base high, set 09-25) before it trades below $2,600. From $2,669.37 that's +$73 up versus -$69 down, so this is a genuine directional call and not a hedge: I am saying the four-day flag resolves upward and the 09-28 dip to 2635 was the shakeout low, not the start of the breakdown. If it trades below $2,600 first, the base has failed, the 2627 higher low is gone, and I added at exactly the wrong moment — my stop at 2547 then handles it and my read of contracting-volume consolidation as accumulation was wrong. If neither triggers, price is still coiling in the 2600-2740 flag and I earn no credit.

decisions.reasoning: My last call was correct: 4h close 2746.04 printed above 2742 with no trade below 2600, so the 2635-2742 base resolved upward. I wanted to add into that and discovered I cannot — I am already at the size cap of a third (0 completed round trips), which is also why the 09-28 add was rejected. So buy is not available and sell makes no sense: daily higher lows 2356/2434/2563/2627/2651/2672 are unbroken, the base high just broke on expanding volume, and the position is +11.9%. Holding a confirmed breakout at max allowed size is the correct and only action. My 2345 stop is 14.5% under spot, so it is not real protection on this leg; the genuine invalidation is a daily close back under 2635.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a 4h close above $2,820 before it prints a 4h close below $2,670. From $2,744.98 that is +$75 against -$75, equidistant, so this is a directional call and not a hedge. I am saying the breakout from the seven-day 2635-2742 base follows through and exceeds the 09-21 swing high of $2,806.69, en route to the measured move near $2,849. If a 4h close below $2,670 comes first, the breakout was a one-bar liquidity grab that failed straight back into the base, my read of the 10-02 expansion as genuine demand was wrong, and the right posture would have been to take the +12% rather than hold. If neither triggers, price is chopping in 2670-2820 and I earn no credit.

decisions.reasoning: My last call lost on the letter: the 10-02 breakout failed back under 2670 within four hours. But the damage was marginal ($2 through the line) and price is now back at 2714, so the structure is unchanged rather than broken. What's in front of me is a 15-day coil: lower highs 2806/2787/2776/2738/2737 against higher lows 2627/2635/2650/2665/2686/2689, with daily range compressed to ~60 from ~110 and volume drying up. That is a symmetrical contraction sitting above a rising base, following a +18% impulse from 2367 to 2806. Coils that form after an impulse resolve with the impulse more often than against it, so I'm betting the break is up. Mechanically I have no choice but hold-or-sell: I'm at the one-third size cap so buys auto-reject. And selling here is the real mistake available to me - I'm only 35.7% exposed at +10.7% in an intact uptrend, already behind a buy-and-hold baseline, and dumping a winner into a tight consolidation pays 0.5% in fees to make that gap permanent.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a daily close above $2,780 before it prints a daily close below $2,655. From $2,714.49 that is +$66 up against -$59 down, and both levels sit outside the 13-day daily-close band of 2668-2726, so this is a call on which side of the coil breaks rather than a straddle on noise. I am saying the apex resolves upward and ETH re-attacks the 09-21 high of $2,806.69. If a daily close below $2,655 comes first, the higher-low sequence (2650/2665/2686) is broken, the coil has resolved down, my read of contraction-after-impulse as accumulation is wrong for the second time in a row, and I should be cutting to cash rather than riding a dead stop at 2345. If neither prints by the deadline, the coil is still coiling past its apex, which is itself informative - a triangle that refuses to break for three weeks is distribution, not accumulation, and I earn no credit.

decisions.reasoning: The three-week coil I was long into resolved DOWN, not up. The 10-07 00:00 4h bar broke every higher low of the structure (2635/2650/2686) in one 109-point, 3.6x-ATR candle on the largest volume in the window, closing near its low. My 10-06 decision pre-committed to cutting rather than riding a dead 2345 stop if a close under 2655 came first, and that is what happened — honoring it. Two straight upside-breakout calls were wrong, which tells me I misread compression-after-impulse as accumulation. Only a third is allowed this wake, so that is the exit: exposure 34.8% -> ~23% for ~$0.30 of fees, while keeping two thirds long from 2452 in case this was a liquidation wick. The coil's measured move (171 height broken at 2635) targets ~2464, which is my own entry — the remaining stake has real downside room.
decisions.expectation: ETH prints a 4h close below $2,525 before it prints a 4h close above $2,700. If neither prints by the deadline, price is chopping in 2,525-2,700 beneath a broken floor and I earn no credit.

Not buying: my two logged losses both came from reading post-impulse weakness as accumulation, and the one call I got right was riding the breakdown. The 85% cash is the real asset and gets deployed when a bid shows up, not into a vertical flush. Data tools returned empty this wake, so this is read off the prompt tables only.
